2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor of the present respondent-opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No.51 of 1998 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Chitalmari for partition, contending inter alia, that one Narayan Chandra Bala was the recorded tenant in S.A. khatian No.125, under Mouza. Khoromkhali of Chitalmari Upazila under Bagerhat District along with his other co-sharers in the suit holding in 50% share comprising an area of 2.01 acres of land. He was also a recorded tenant in 3/4 share comprising an area of 1.78 acres of land in S.A. khatian No.I99 of the same Mouza. The father of Narayan Chandra namely Bhaggya Dhar Bala during his life time obtained 0.52 acres of land in plot No.202 appertaining to C.S. khatian No.73 corresponding to S.A. khatian No.201 and 299 from a recorded tenant of the suit holding one Malek Mia and others. Thereafter, the father of the plaintiffs erected his dwelling but on 0.52 acres of land and subsequently died leaving behind his son Narayan Chandra Bala. During peaceful possession of the plaintiffs while one Darikanath Bala tried to dispossess the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs filed a civil suit which was decreed in favour of the plaintiffs up to the appellate court. In the subsequent record of right the land of plot No.202 of C.S. khatian No.73 while not recorded in the name of Narayan, he filed a suit being Title Suit No.285 of 1985 and during pendency of that suit he died leaving behind two sons Bankim Chandra Bala and Suklal Bala. Bankim Chandra in the aforesaid suit alleged that he is the sole successor of his father Narayan Chandra Bala. At the death of Suklal, Bankim Chandra did not substitute the heirs of Suklal. Subsequently, Bankim Chandra by a registered sub-kabala dated 20.06.1990 transferred 0.16 acres of land from plot No.201 and .06 acres of land from plot No. 197 of S.A. khatian No.199 and 0.10 acres of land from plot No.202 of S.A. khatian No.201/299 measuring the total land 0.12 acres in favour of the plaintiffs and delivered possession therein. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that Suklal transferred 0.25 acres of land of the suit holding in favour of one Moazzem Hossain and Moniruzzaman by a registered kabala dated .24.11.1985, who subsequently transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs by a registered transfer deed dated 15.06.1988. In this way; the plaintiffs after acquiring right, title, interest and possession in the land measuring 0.50 acres by a mutation proceedings mutated their names and opened a separate khatian being No.199/1. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that Suklal by a kabala dated 12.04.1997 transferred 0.26 acres of land from suit plot No.202 in favour of the plaintiffs and thereafter the plaintiffs acquired in all 0.86 acres of land in the suit holding and Civil Suit being No.59 of 1997 which was filed against the decree of Title Suit No.285 of 1985 was dismissed for default and that the defendant No.1 created a false nadabi-paira from Suklal on 16.10.1997 and that due to the difficulty of ejmali possession with the defendants the plaintiffs requested the defendants for amicable partition but they refused, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for partition in respect of 0.86 acres of land in the suit holding. 

 11. Both the parties to the suit, to substantiate their respective claim have adduced witnesses and the plaintiffs have examined 05(five) witnesses and submitted their basic documents marked as exhibits. On the other hand, the defendant-petitioner has examined 03 witnesses in support of his case and submitted some documentary evidence, which are also have been marked as exhibits by the learned trial court. It is the concurrent findings and decisions of both the courts below that in the lands of S.A. khatians No. 201, 299, 199 and 125 the predecessors of the parties have got their interest and title: In the land measuring 1.78 acres the predecessor of the parties namely Narayan Chandra had 1.1866 acres of land corresponding to S.A. khatian No.199 and two sons at the demise of their father acquired .59333 acres of land. It further appears from the observation and findings of the courts below that the learned trial court under the ambit of section 73 of the Evidence Act, 1872 compared the signature of Suklal Bala and scrutinized the signature with the registered sub-kabala deed dated 24.12.1985 with the signature as it appears in kabala deed dated 12.04.1996' which has been marked as Exhibit-5 and after comparison of the signatures, conclusively held that the signatures as it appears with the deed under challenge in Title Suit No.82 of 1998 is the product of same individual and it is decided concurrently by the trial court as well as the Appellate Court that the allegation of forgery as raised from the side of the defendant-petitioner is not proved by any tangible evidence and as a result the plaintiffs to the suit obtained 0.26 acres of land in the suit plot No.202 by virtue of the kabala deed dated 12.04.1997 and the plaintiffs have succeeded to establish their plaint case by cogent evidence and that they have title and possession to the extent of 0.22 acres of land in suit plot No.197 and 201 by the purchase deed dated 20.06.1990. 

 17. Vis-à-vis; the D:W.1 of the defendant, who is the defendant No.1 himself Bankim Chandra Bala in his testimony testified that he is the defendant to the suit and the total land of plot No.232 of the C.S. khatian No.73 consists of 52 decimals originally belonged to one Abdul Goni and Bhaggya Dhar was a tenant under him. This witness testified in support of his written statement. 

 21. During cross-examination this witness frankly testified that in the khatian No.299 total quantum of land is 3.22 acres and beside plot No.202 he cannot recollect anything about the land of remaining plots.
